THREAT.why: A threatened punishment can make the moment feel less safe and raise the tension.
THREAT.tryInstead: You are upset, {childName}. I am right here. {limit}.

BRIBE.why: A new reward may stop the crying now, but it makes the next limit harder to hold.
BRIBE.tryInstead: You really wanted {wants}. {limit}. I will stay close.

YELL.why: A raised voice adds intensity when the child is already overwhelmed.
YELL.tryInstead: I am right here, {childName}. You are upset. {limit}.

SHAME.why: Labels and comparisons can hurt connection instead of showing the child what to do.
SHAME.tryInstead: You feel frustrated. I am here with you. {limit}.

DISMISS.why: Telling a feeling to go away can leave the child feeling unheard.
DISMISS.tryInstead: You really wanted {wants}. It is hard. {limit}.

QUESTION_COMMAND.why: A question can make a necessary instruction sound optional.
QUESTION_COMMAND.tryInstead: You are upset. I am right here. {limit}. Hold my hand.

LECTURE.why: Long explanations are hard to take in while feelings are this strong.
LECTURE.tryInstead: You are upset. I am here. {limit}.

NEGATIVE_COMMAND.why: Saying what not to do leaves the next helpful action unclear.
NEGATIVE_COMMAND.tryInstead: You are frustrated. I am here. Hold my hand. {limit}.

VAGUE_COMMAND.why: A broad instruction does not give the child a clear next step.
VAGUE_COMMAND.tryInstead: You are upset. I am here. Hold my hand. {limit}.

GIVE_IN.why: The crying stopped because the limit changed, rather than because the child practised handling it.
GIVE_IN.tryInstead: You really wanted {wants}. I am right here. {limit}.

NO_RESPONSE.why: The child did not hear a response or feel your presence in that moment.
NO_RESPONSE.tryInstead: I am here, {childName}. You are upset. {limit}.
